environment.database: Oracle AI Database 26ai Free Release 23.26.3.0.0 - Develop, Learn, and Run for Free Version 23.26.3.0.0

steps.name: install: clean schema and APEX application
unit tests: Paillier library and election API

gate.title: Test vectors
gate.statement: The Java verifier in the database reproduced 162/162 hashes of the browser byte for byte, over 18 fixed ballots in 2 key sizes (512 and 2048 bits), agreed with the browser on every verdict (6 accepted, 12 rejected) and verified 18/18 WebCrypto signatures. 6 altered vectors were all caught.

hypotheses.title: Soundness
hypotheses.statement: The database rejected 8 of 8 dishonest ballots pasted in the browser console, among them the ballot of 1000 votes and the balanced [3, -2, 0] that Layer 1 accepted, 3 of 3 replays, and 100 of 100 valid ballots with one digit changed. The tally stayed A=5  B=3  C=2: the honest ballots and the control.

hypotheses.title: Completeness
hypotheses.statement: 100 random elections with 2048-bit keys: 520 of 520 honest ballots accepted, all 520 counted after a second verification, and the decrypted tally equal to the true result in 100 of 100. A dishonest ballot placed among honest ones was refused.

hypotheses.title: Integrity
hypotheses.statement: The owner and an account with the DBA role had 10 of 10 UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and MERGE statements refused each, where an ordinary copy of the table accepted them. 5 of 5 forged or unsigned ballots were rejected. The DBA could still INSERT 3 forged ballots; the tally counted none of them (6 counted, 3 rejected) and the chain verified over 1651 rows.

hypotheses.title: What still breaks
hypotheses.statement: All 7 limits held up in the lab: the key holder read 6 of 6 ballots with the voter code next to each; the hidden insert time re-linked 6 of 6; a DBA voted in the name of a registered voter with one UPDATE; a DBA dropped and rebuilt the tables without one ballot and the chain still verified; the owner made the tally refuse 2 honest ballots (this one is reported by the tally); a substituted vote.js read the choice; the verifier was replaced without a trace in the tables.

hypotheses.title: Cost
hypotheses.statement: Measured: proofs add 3808 hexadecimal characters to a ballot; encrypting and proving takes a median 283 ms in the browser and casting 1032 ms from the click to the receipt (Layer 1: 289 ms); the database verifies one ballot in 641 ms; the tally of 10000 voters takes 104.7 min against 4.9 s in Layer 1.
